==== src/VerifySample.Tests/ModuleInitializer.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=EntityFramework&min=EntityFramework&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Metadata;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Verify.EntityFramework: the model is read once here so IgnoreNavigationProperties() can be
        // called without arguments, and so navigation properties stay out of entity snapshots.
        VerifyEntityFramework.Initialize(GetDbModel());

        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }

    // Builds a context against a connection string that is never opened, purely to read the model.
    static IModel GetDbModel()
    {
        var options = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<SampleDbContext>();
        options.UseSqlServer("fake");
        using var data = new SampleDbContext(options.Options);
        return data.Model;
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/EntityFrameworkTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=EntityFramework&min=EntityFramework&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;

// Verify.EntityFramework (EF Core): Records the SQL EF Core runs, snapshots ChangeTracker state, and turns an IQueryable into readable SQL.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.EntityFramework
// Note: EnableRecording() belongs in test code only: it attaches an interceptor to every command.
// Note: Recording.Start() can be called on several contexts built from the same options, and the
// entries are aggregated.
// Note: Testing through WebApplicationFactory needs a named recording, Recording.Start(name) and
// Recording.Stop(name), and the entries have to be passed to Verify explicitly.
// Note: The samples point at a local SQL Server. Selecting LocalDb as well generates a database
// per test instead.
public class EntityFrameworkTests
{
    // Everything EF runs between Recording.Start() and the verification is added to the
    // snapshot under the name ef, with the command text, its type and the transaction state.
    // Nothing needs to be passed to Verify: recorded entries are included on their own.
    [Fact]
    public async Task RecordCommands()
    {
        await using var data = NewContext();
        Recording.Start();

        await data
            .Companies
            .Where(_ => _.Name == "Title")
            .ToListAsync();

        await Verify();
    }

    // Verifying an IQueryable writes two snapshots: a .verified.txt with the materialized
    // results, and a .verified.sql with the SQL EF would run. The query is not executed for the
    // SQL file, so a broken query still shows up as a diff rather than as an exception.
    [Fact]
    public async Task Queryable()
    {
        await using var data = NewContext();
        var queryable = data
            .Companies
            .Where(_ => _.Name == "Title");
        await Verify(queryable);
    }

    // EnableRecording attaches the interceptor, and belongs only in test code.
    static SampleDbContext NewContext()
    {
        var builder = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<SampleDbContext>();
        builder.UseSqlServer("Server=(local);Database=Sample;Integrated Security=true;Encrypt=false");
        builder.EnableRecording();
        return new(builder.Options);
    }
}
